title: These Unemployment Numbers Are Going Up
gist: Gavekal Dragonomics argues China's headline unemployment rates -- first the old 'registered' urban rate pinned near 4%, now the 'surveyed' rate pinned near 5% -- have conveyed essentially no information about actual labor-market swings, because coverage and reporting incentives suppress variation. Note: this record is a short teaser (~170 words); the title's claim that the numbers are 'going up' is not substantiated in the available text, which stops at the critique of the indicators before the paywall.

insights.claim: China's official unemployment rate is, on Gavekal Dragonomics' view, the single Chinese economic statistic with the longest track record of being useless for reading the economy.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Investors modelling Chinese consumption or policy reaction functions off the headline jobless rate are anchoring on a series with near-zero information content; substitute alternative labor proxies.
insights.quote: There may be no Chinese economic statistic with a longer history of being utterly useless than the unemployment rate.
insights.locator: There may be no Chinese economic statistic

insights.claim: For decades China published only a 'registered' urban unemployment rate that stayed near 4% and failed to move through the state-enterprise layoffs or the 2008 global financial crisis.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A series that did not register two of the largest labor shocks in modern Chinese history cannot be used to time or size a current downturn.
insights.quote: amazingly steady around 4%, failing to reflect massive shocks like the layoffs from state enterprises or the 2008 global financial crisis
insights.locator: For decades, China reported only a “registered” urban unemployment rate

insights.claim: The registered rate's flatness is attributed to design and incentives -- it covered only a restricted group with access to official unemployment benefits, a population the authorities had strong reasons to keep small.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A reusable screen for Chinese data: where the reported population is also the population that triggers a fiscal obligation, expect the print to be administratively managed rather than measured.
insights.quote: it covered only a restricted group with access to official unemployment benefits, whose numbers the authorities had strong incentives to control
insights.locator: That was probably because it covered only a restricted group

insights.claim: The replacement 'surveyed' unemployment rate has broader coverage and a definition closer to international standards, yet apart from a brief pandemic spike it has also been remarkably steady around 5%.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Methodological reform did not restore signal -- do not treat the post-reform series as a clean break that is now tradable.
insights.quote: But aside from a brief spike during the pandemic, that rate has also been amazingly steady around 5%.
insights.locator: After years of criticism, that indicator was replaced

insights.claim: Both of China's headline unemployment measures, despite their technical differences, have in practice delivered little information about changes in the job market -- so labor-market deterioration must be inferred from other indicators rather than the headline rate.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Build the China labor view from wage growth, migrant employment, hiring surveys and youth-unemployment sub-series; a stable headline print is not evidence of a stable job market and should not be read as an argument against stimulus.
insights.quote: Despite their technical differences, both headline unemployment rates have in practice delivered little information about changes in the job market.
